"""Shared fixtures and the ``compare_screenshot`` helper for visual tests.

Visual regression testing captures a screenshot of a GUI component and
compares it pixel-for-pixel against a committed *golden* reference image.
The test fails when the difference exceeds a threshold, which catches
unintended layout/paint changes that ordinary assertions miss.

Capture works for two kinds of targets:

* ``QWidget`` (e.g. ``MainWindow``, ``CanvasView``) — grabbed with
  ``QWidget.grab()``.
* ``QGraphicsItem`` (the hardware blocks) — blocks are scene items, not
  widgets, so they have no ``grab()``/``show()``. They are rendered through
  a ``QGraphicsScene`` instead.

The first run auto-creates any missing golden, so a fresh test passes once
and then guards against regressions on every later run.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import os
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pytest
from PIL import Image, ImageChops
from PyQt6.QtCore import QRectF, Qt
from PyQt6.QtGui import QImage, QPainter
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QGraphicsItem, QGraphicsScene, QWidget

GOLDEN_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "golden"
DIFF_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "diffs"
DIFF_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

# Max allowed RMS pixel difference (0-255 per channel, averaged over the
# image). 0 = pixel perfect; 5 tolerates minor antialiasing/font differences
# between machines without hiding real layout changes.
DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = 5


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def qapp():
    """Single QApplication for the whole test session.

    The repository's top-level ``tests/conftest.py`` forces
    ``QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`` before any Qt import, so this works
    headlessly (CI/EC2) with no display.
    """
    app = QApplication.instance() or QApplication([])
    yield app


def _qimage_to_pil(qimage: QImage) -> Image.Image:
    """Convert a ``QImage`` to a PIL RGB image.

    Converting to RGBA8888 first gives a known channel order and a tightly
    packed buffer (no row padding), so the same code works regardless of the
    platform's native pixmap format.
    """
    qimage = qimage.convertToFormat(QImage.Format.Format_RGBA8888)
    width, height = qimage.width(), qimage.height()
    ptr = qimage.bits()
    ptr.setsize(qimage.sizeInBytes())
    arr = np.frombuffer(ptr, dtype=np.uint8).reshape((height, width, 4))
    return Image.fromarray(arr, mode="RGBA").convert("RGB")


def _capture_graphics_item(item: QGraphicsItem) -> QImage:
    """Render a single ``QGraphicsItem`` (a hardware block) to a ``QImage``.

    The item is rendered alone on a white background so the golden captures
    just the block — not the canvas grid or any neighbouring blocks. A
    detached item is parked in a temporary plain scene for the render and
    removed again afterwards so the caller's object is left untouched.
    """
    temp_scene = None
    scene = item.scene()
    if scene is None:
        temp_scene = QGraphicsScene()
        temp_scene.addItem(item)
        scene = temp_scene

    source = item.mapToScene(item.boundingRect()).boundingRect()
    width, height = int(source.width()), int(source.height())
    image = QImage(width, height, QImage.Format.Format_ARGB32)
    image.fill(Qt.GlobalColor.white)

    painter = QPainter(image)
    painter.setRenderHint(QPainter.RenderHint.Antialiasing)
    scene.render(painter, QRectF(0, 0, width, height), source)
    painter.end()

    if temp_scene is not None:
        temp_scene.removeItem(item)
    return image


def _capture(target) -> QImage:
    """Capture a screenshot of a QWidget or a QGraphicsItem."""
    if isinstance(target, QWidget):
        return target.grab().toImage()
    if isinstance(target, QGraphicsItem):
        return _capture_graphics_item(target)
    raise TypeError(
        f"compare_screenshot expects a QWidget or QGraphicsItem, got {type(target)!r}"
    )


def compare_screenshot(target, name: str,
                       threshold: int = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD,
                       update_golden: bool = False) -> None:
    """Screenshot ``target`` and assert it matches ``golden/<name>.png``.

    Args:
        target:        a ``QWidget`` or ``QGraphicsItem`` to screenshot.
        name:          golden filename stem, e.g. ``"main_window"``.
        threshold:     max allowed RMS pixel difference (default 5).
        update_golden: force-save the screenshot as the new golden. Also
                       triggered by the ``UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`` environment
                       variable so references can be refreshed in bulk after
                       an intentional UI change.

    The golden is auto-created when missing (first run), so a new test passes
    once and then guards against regressions. On failure the actual and an
    amplified diff image are written to ``tests/visual/diffs/`` and the
    assertion message explains how to accept the change.
    """
    golden_path = GOLDEN_DIR / f"{name}.png"
    diff_path = DIFF_DIR / f"{name}_diff.png"
    actual_path = DIFF_DIR / f"{name}_actual.png"

    update_golden = update_golden or os.environ.get("UPDATE_GOLDEN", "0") == "1"

    actual = _qimage_to_pil(_capture(target))

    if update_golden or not golden_path.exists():
        GOLDEN_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        actual.save(golden_path)
        print(f"Golden image saved: {golden_path}")
        return

    golden = Image.open(golden_path).convert("RGB")

    assert actual.size == golden.size, (
        f"Screenshot size changed: expected {golden.size}, got {actual.size}.\n"
        f"If intentional, delete {golden_path} and re-run to regenerate."
    )

    diff = ImageChops.difference(actual, golden)
    rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(np.asarray(diff, dtype=float) ** 2)))

    if rms > threshold:
        actual.save(actual_path)
        # Amplify the diff 10x so small differences are visible to a human.
        amplified = Image.fromarray(
            np.clip(np.asarray(diff) * 10, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)
        )
        amplified.save(diff_path)
        raise AssertionError(
            f"Visual regression: '{name}' pixel RMS={rms:.2f} > threshold={threshold}\n"
            f"  Golden: {golden_path}\n"
            f"  Actual: {actual_path}\n"
            f"  Diff:   {diff_path}  (amplified 10x)\n"
            f"If intentional: review the actual image, then\n"
            f"  cp {actual_path} {golden_path} && git add {golden_path}"
        )

    print(f"Visual OK: '{name}' RMS={rms:.2f} (threshold={threshold})")

"""Visual + smoke tests for the Silmulator main window.

These run headlessly: the repository's top-level ``tests/conftest.py`` sets
``QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen`` before Qt is imported, and on EC2 pytest-xvfb
provides a virtual display, so no ``DISPLAY`` needs to be set by hand.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from silmulator.gui.main_window import MainWindow

from .conftest import compare_screenshot

# The window resizes itself to 1400x900; it must never render smaller than
# this usable minimum or docks/toolbar controls get clipped.
MIN_WIDTH = 800
MIN_HEIGHT = 600


def test_main_window_opens(qapp, qtbot):
    """Main window renders without crashing and matches the golden image."""
    window = MainWindow()
    qtbot.addWidget(window)
    window.show()
    qtbot.waitExposed(window, timeout=5000)
    qapp.processEvents()  # flush pending layout/paint events before grabbing
    compare_screenshot(window, "main_window")


def test_main_window_title(qapp, qtbot):
    """Window title identifies the app.

    The issue specifies ``== "Silmulator"``, but the real window appends a
    subtitle (``"Silmulator — SIL/HIL/CIL Hardware Simulator"``). Asserting
    the prefix honours the intent (the window is identifiably Silmulator)
    without coupling the test to the exact subtitle wording.
    """
    window = MainWindow()
    qtbot.addWidget(window)
    assert window.windowTitle().startswith("Silmulator")


def test_main_window_minimum_size(qapp, qtbot):
    """Window opens at least 800x600 so no controls are clipped."""
    window = MainWindow()
    qtbot.addWidget(window)
    window.show()
    qtbot.waitExposed(window, timeout=5000)
    qapp.processEvents()
    assert window.width() >= MIN_WIDTH
    assert window.height() >= MIN_HEIGHT

"""Visual tests: every built-in hardware block renders correctly.

Blocks are ``QGraphicsItem``s, not ``QWidget``s, so they cannot be
``show()``/``waitExposed``-ed like the main window — ``compare_screenshot``
renders them through a ``QGraphicsScene`` instead (see conftest). Each block
is captured in its default, unconfigured state.

One golden per block type. Parametrised over the built-in types (following
the existing pattern in ``tests/test_block_creation.py``) so adding a new
built-in block automatically gets a render test once it is listed here.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from silmulator.gui.canvas import BLOCK_REGISTRY

from .conftest import compare_screenshot

# device_type (registry key) -> golden image stem.
BUILTIN_BLOCKS = {
    "Oscilloscope": "oscilloscope_block",
    "Power Supply": "psu_block",
    "Function Generator": "function_generator_block",
    "Multimeter": "multimeter_block",
    "MSP430": "msp430_block",
    "Code Input": "code_input_block",
}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("device_type,golden", list(BUILTIN_BLOCKS.items()))
def test_block_renders(qapp, device_type, golden):
    """Each built-in block renders to its golden image in default state."""
    cls = BLOCK_REGISTRY.get(device_type)
    if cls is None:
        pytest.skip(f"block type {device_type!r} not registered")
    block = cls()
    qapp.processEvents()
    compare_screenshot(block, golden)

"""Multimeter hardware block for the GUI canvas."""

from __future__ import annotations
from PyQt6.QtCore import QRectF, Qt
from PyQt6.QtGui import QPainter, QColor, QPen, QBrush, QFont
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QMenu

from silmulator.gui.blocks.base_block import BaseBlock
from silmulator.devices.multimeter import Multimeter


class MultimeterBlock(BaseBlock):
    """Visual representation of the digital multimeter simulator."""

    BLOCK_WIDTH = 200
    BLOCK_HEIGHT = 160
    HEADER_COLOR = QColor(80, 50, 120)
    BODY_COLOR = QColor(240, 235, 250)

    FUNC_LABELS = {
        "VOLT:DC": ("VDC", "V"),
        "VOLT:AC": ("VAC", "V"),
        "CURR:DC": ("ADC", "A"),
        "CURR:AC": ("AAC", "A"),
        "RES": ("Ω", "Ω"),
        "FRES": ("4WΩ", "Ω"),
        "FREQ": ("FREQ", "Hz"),
        "PER": ("PERIOD", "s"),
        "CONT": ("CONT", "Ω"),
        "DIOD": ("DIODE", "V"),
        "TEMP": ("TEMP", "°C"),
    }

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__(Multimeter(), "Multimeter")
        self._last_reading: float = 0.0

    @property
    def dmm(self) -> Multimeter:
        return self.device  # type: ignore

    def _setup_ports(self) -> None:
        self.add_port("HI", "HI", 0.5, 1.0)
        self.add_port("LO", "LO", 0.7, 1.0)
        self.add_port("CURR_IN", "A", 0.3, 1.0)
        self.add_port("GUARD", "G", 0.0, 0.7)

    def _paint_content(self, painter: QPainter, rect: QRectF) -> None:
        dmm = self.dmm

        # Display screen
        disp_rect = QRectF(rect.x() + 10, self.TITLE_HEIGHT + 8,
                           rect.width() - 20, 70)
        painter.setBrush(QBrush(QColor(0, 30, 0)))
        painter.setPen(QPen(QColor(0, 80, 0), 1))
        painter.drawRect(disp_rect)

        # Read a fresh measurement for display
        func = dmm.config.function
        reading = dmm._get_reading(func)
        self._last_reading = reading

        # Main display value (7-segment style)
        func_label, unit = self.FUNC_LABELS.get(func, ("???", ""))
        disp_font = QFont("Consolas", 20, QFont.Weight.Bold)
        painter.setFont(disp_font)
        painter.setPen(QPen(QColor(0, 255, 60)))
        reading_str = _format_reading(reading, func)
        painter.drawText(disp_rect, Qt.AlignmentFlag.AlignCenter, reading_str)

        # Function label
        small_font = QFont("Consolas", 8)
        painter.setFont(small_font)
        painter.setPen(QPen(QColor(0, 200, 60)))
        painter.drawText(
            QRectF(disp_rect.x() + 4, disp_rect.y() + 4, 60, 16),
            Qt.AlignmentFlag.AlignLeft | Qt.AlignmentFlag.AlignTop,
            func_label
        )
        painter.drawText(
            QRectF(disp_rect.right() - 30, disp_rect.y() + 4, 26, 16),
            Qt.AlignmentFlag.AlignRight | Qt.AlignmentFlag.AlignTop,
            unit
        )

        # Config info
        info_font = QFont("Consolas", 7)
        painter.setFont(info_font)
        painter.setPen(QPen(QColor(80, 80, 80)))
        range_str = "AUTO" if dmm.config.auto_range else f"{dmm.config.range:.3g}"
        nplc_str = f"NPLC:{dmm.config.nplc}"
        painter.drawText(int(rect.x() + 10), int(disp_rect.bottom() + 14),
                         f"Range:{range_str}  {nplc_str}")
        painter.drawText(int(rect.x() + 10), int(disp_rect.bottom() + 26),
                         f"Trig:{dmm.trigger.source}  Samp:{dmm.sample.count}")

    def _add_device_menu_actions(self, menu: QMenu) -> None:
        func_menu = menu.addMenu("Set Function")
        funcs = [
            ("Voltage DC", "MEAS:VOLT:DC"),
            ("Voltage AC", "MEAS:VOLT:AC"),
            ("Current DC", "MEAS:CURR:DC"),
            ("Resistance", "MEAS:RES"),
            ("4-Wire Resistance", "MEAS:FRES"),
            ("Frequency", "MEAS:FREQ"),
            ("Diode", "MEAS:DIOD"),
            ("Temperature", "MEAS:TEMP"),
        ]
        for label, cmd in funcs:
            func_menu.addAction(label, lambda c=cmd: self.send_command(c))

    def measure(self, function: str = None) -> float:
        """Programmatic measurement — returns numeric reading."""
        func = function or self.dmm.config.function

        elif abs_v >= 10:

        elif abs_v >= 1:
            return f"{value:+.7f}"
        else:

    elif func in ("CURR:DC", "CURR:AC"):
        if abs_v >= 1:
            return f"{value:+.5f}"
        elif abs_v >= 0.1:
            return f"{value:+.6f}"
        else:
            return f"{value:+.7f}"
    elif func in ("RES", "FRES", "CONT"):
        if abs_v >= 1e6:
            return f"{value / 1e6:+.5f}M"
        elif abs_v >= 1e3:
            return f"{value / 1e3:+.5f}k"
        else:
            return f"{value:+.5f}"
    elif func == "FREQ":
        if abs_v >= 1e6:
            return f"{value / 1e6:.5f}M"
        elif abs_v >= 1e3:
            return f"{value / 1e3:.5f}k"
        else:
            return f"{value:.5f}"
    else:

``test_canvas_with_psu_block`` is a real interaction test: it clicks the

from PyQt6.QtCore import Qt
from PyQt6.QtWidgets import QPushButton

from silmulator.gui.main_window import MainWindow

    """Return the toolbar button that adds the given block type."""

            return button
    raise AssertionError(f"no palette button labelled {label!r}")

    window = MainWindow()
    window.resize(WINDOW_WIDTH, WINDOW_HEIGHT)
    qtbot.addWidget(window)
    window.show()
    qtbot.waitExposed(window, timeout=5000)
    qapp.processEvents()
    assert window.canvas.blocks == []
    compare_screenshot(window.canvas_view, "canvas_empty")


def test_canvas_with_psu_block(qapp, qtbot):
    """Clicking the PSU palette button adds a Power Supply block to the canvas."""
    window = MainWindow()

# Silmulator

**SIL/HIL/CIL Hardware Simulator** — A PyQt6 GUI application for debugging embedded software against simulated lab instruments that behave per their real device specifications.

## Documentation

| Guide | Description |
|---|---|
| [User Guide](docs/user_guide.md) | Installation, quick start, virtual hardware reference, troubleshooting |
| [Developer Guide](docs/developer_guide.md) | Architecture, device layer, GUI layer, adding devices |
| [Adding Blocks](docs/adding_blocks.md) | Step-by-step guide to creating new hardware blocks |
| [Architecture Diagrams](docs/architecture.md) | Mermaid diagrams: system overview, data flow, class hierarchy |
| [Docker Guide](docker/README.md) | Browser (NoVNC) and native window Docker usage |
| [C++ Core](cpp_core/README.md) | SCPI parser build, API reference, Doxygen instructions |
| [Python Package](silmulator/README.md) | Package structure, library API reference |
| [Word User Guide](docs/Silmulator_User_Guide.docx) | Official Microsoft Word version for distribution |

## Overview

Silmulator provides a drag-and-drop canvas where you place virtual hardware blocks — oscilloscopes, power supplies, function generators, multimeters, and MSP430 microcontrollers — connect them with virtual wires, and interact with them using real SCPI commands. A code-input block parses your C/C++/Python source and routes the SCPI calls to the connected devices.

This lets you test and debug measurement code **without physical hardware**, catching command errors and response-handling bugs at your desk.

## Architecture

```
Silmulator/
├── main.py                        # CLI entry point
├── setup.py                       # pip install support
├── requirements.txt               # Python dependencies
├── CMakeLists.txt                 # C++ build root
│
├── cpp_core/                      # High-performance C++ SCPI parser
│   ├── CMakeLists.txt
│   ├── include/
│   │   ├── scpi_parser.h          # Parser class declaration
│   │   └── scpi_types.h           # ScpiCommand, ScpiToken, etc.
│   └── src/
│       ├── scpi_parser.cpp        # Parser implementation
│       └── bindings.cpp           # pybind11 Python bindings
│
└── silmulator/                    # Python package
    ├── app.py                     # Application entry point
    ├── scpi/
    │   └── parser.py              # Pure-Python SCPI parser (fallback)
    ├── devices/
    │   ├── base_device.py         # Abstract SCPI device base
    │   ├── oscilloscope.py        # Tektronix MSO54-compatible
    │   ├── power_supply.py        # Keysight E36312A-compatible
    │   ├── function_generator.py  # Keysight 33522B-compatible
    │   ├── multimeter.py          # Keysight 34401A-compatible
    │   └── msp430.py              # TI MSP430FR5994-compatible
    ├── gui/
    │   ├── main_window.py         # PyQt6 main window
    │   ├── canvas.py              # Drag-and-drop scene + view
    │   └── blocks/
    │       ├── base_block.py      # Abstract block base class
    │       ├── oscilloscope_block.py
    │       ├── power_supply_block.py
    │       ├── function_generator_block.py
    │       ├── multimeter_block.py
    │       ├── msp430_block.py
    │       └── code_input_block.py
    ├── code_parser/
    │   └── base_parser.py         # C/C++/Python SCPI extractor
    └── utils/
        ├── waveform.py            # Waveform generation (numpy)
        └── signals.py             # Qt signal bus
```

## Simulated Instruments

### Oscilloscope (Tektronix MSO54-compatible)
- 4 analog channels (CH1–CH4)
- Full `ACQ`, `CH`, `CURSOR`, `DATA`, `DISPLAY`, `HORIZONTAL`, `MEASUREMENT`, `SELECT`, `TRIGGER`, `WFMPRE` command trees
- Waveform generation and `CURVE?` data transfer (ASCII and binary encoding)
- Live waveform injection via `inject_waveform(source, array)`
- 8 configurable measurements: FREQUENCY, PERIOD, AMPLITUDE, RMS, MEAN, HIGH, LOW, PK2PK, RISE, FALL, PDUTY, NDUTY

### Power Supply (Keysight E36312A-compatible)
- 3 independent channels
- `SOURCE:VOLTAGE`, `SOURCE:CURRENT`, `OUTPUT`, `MEASURE`, `TRIGGER`, `INSTRUMENT` command trees
- OVP/OCP protection simulation
- `APPLY` combined set command
- Channel-by-channel tracking mode

### Function Generator (Keysight 33522B-compatible)
- 2 independent channels (SOURCE1, SOURCE2)
- Functions: SIN, SQU, RAMP, PULS, NOIS, DC, USER, ARB
- AM, FM, PM, PWM modulation
- Burst and sweep modes
- Arbitrary waveform catalog

### Multimeter (Keysight 34401A-compatible)
- Functions: VOLT:DC, VOLT:AC, CURR:DC, CURR:AC, RES, FRES, FREQ, PER, CONT, DIOD, TEMP
- `CONFIGURE`, `MEASURE`, `READ`, `FETCH`, `INITIATE` modes
- `CALCULATE` (null, limits, dB, statistics)
- `TRIGGER` and `SAMPLE` subsystems
- `DATA` buffer with `INITIATE`/`FETCH` workflow
- Measurement injection via `inject(function, value)`

### MSP430 (TI MSP430FR5994-compatible)
- 8 GPIO ports (P1–P8) with direction, pull-up/down, interrupt control
- 12-channel 12-bit ADC with voltage injection
- 3x Timer_A, 1x Timer_B with capture-compare
- 4x UART (eUSCI_A) with full serial config
- 2x SPI (eUSCI_B) with CPOL/CPHA and transfer simulation
- 4x I2C with address, frequency, master/slave modes
- Unified Clock System (DCO, LFXT, SMCLK, MCLK, ACLK)
- Power management modes (AM, LPM0–LPM4.5)
- 16-register CPU state, PC control, memory map read/write

## SCPI Command Examples

```python
from silmulator.devices import Oscilloscope, PowerSupply, FunctionGenerator

# Oscilloscope
osc = Oscilloscope()
osc.process("CH1:SCALE 0.5")           # 500mV/div
osc.process("HOR:SCALE 1E-3")          # 1ms/div
osc.process("TRIG:A:EDGE:SOURCE CH1")
osc.process("TRIG:A:LEVEL 1.5")
osc.process("ACQ:STATE 1")             # Run
freq = osc.process("MEASUREMENT:MEAS1:TYPE FREQUENCY; VALUE?")
data = osc.process("CURVE?")           # Get waveform data

# Power Supply
psu = PowerSupply()
psu.process("INST:NSEL 1")
psu.process("VOLT 3.3")
psu.process("CURR 1.0")
psu.process("OUTP ON")
voltage = psu.process("MEAS:VOLT:DC?")

# Function Generator
fgen = FunctionGenerator()
fgen.process("SOURCE1:FUNC SIN")
fgen.process("SOURCE1:FREQ 1000")
fgen.process("SOURCE1:VOLT 2.0")
fgen.process("OUTPUT1 ON")

# MSP430
mcu = MSP430()
mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION 0xFF")  # All outputs
mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:OUTPUT 0x01")     # P1.0 HIGH
mcu.process("ADC:CHANNEL0:INJECT 1.65")  # Inject 1.65V
raw = mcu.process("ADC:CONVERT 0")       # Read raw ADC value
```

## C++ Core

The C++ SCPI parser (`cpp_core/`) provides a high-performance parsing backend with pybind11 Python bindings. It is optional — the pure-Python `silmulator/scpi/parser.py` is used automatically when the C++ extension is not built.

### Building the C++ extension

```bash
mkdir build && cd build
cmake ..
make -j4
# Copy the resulting scpi_core.so to silmulator/scpi/
```

## Code Parser

The `CodeInputBlock` on the canvas parses C, C++, or Python source code to extract SCPI command strings:

**Recognized C/C++ patterns:**
```c
viWrite(session, "VOLT 5.0");
viQueryf(session, "MEAS:VOLT:DC?", result);
visa_write(dev, "OUTP ON");
scpi_send(handle, "ACQ:STATE 1");
ibwrt(dev, "TRIG:A:LEVEL 1.5");
```

**Recognized Python patterns:**
```python
inst.write("VOLT 5.0")
result = inst.query("MEAS:VOLT:DC?")
rm.open_resource("GPIB::1").write("OUTP ON")
```

## GUI Usage

1. **Launch:** `python main.py`
2. **Add blocks:** Double-click items in the Library panel, or click toolbar buttons
3. **Connect blocks:** Click a port circle on one block, drag to a port on another
4. **Send commands:** Select a block → right-click → "Send SCPI command", or use the SCPI Console at the bottom
5. **Paste code:** Add a "Code Input" block → double-click to open the editor → paste your C/C++/Python code → click "Parse" to extract SCPI commands
6. **Run commands:** After connecting a Code Input block to hardware blocks, right-click → "Run parsed commands"
7. **Save/Load layouts:** File → Save (`.sil` JSON format)

### Keyboard shortcuts

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `Delete` | Remove selected blocks |
| `Ctrl+A` | Select all |
| `Ctrl+N` | New canvas |
| `Ctrl+O` | Open layout |
| `Ctrl+S` | Save layout |
| `Ctrl+0` | Reset zoom |
| `Ctrl+Shift+F` | Fit all blocks in view |
| Middle mouse drag | Pan |
| Scroll wheel | Zoom in/out |

## Running Tests

```bash
# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Run all tests
python -m pytest tests/ -v

# Run specific device tests
python -m pytest tests/test_oscilloscope.py -v
python -m pytest tests/test_power_supply.py -v
python -m pytest tests/test_function_generator.py -v
python -m pytest tests/test_multimeter.py -v
python -m pytest tests/test_msp430.py -v
python -m pytest tests/test_scpi_parser.py -v
```

## Requirements

- Python 3.9+
- PyQt6 >= 6.4.0
- numpy >= 1.24.0
- scipy >= 1.10.0

Optional (for C++ parser):
- CMake >= 3.16
- pybind11 >= 2.10.0
- C++17 compiler (GCC, Clang, or MSVC)

## Design Decisions

**SCPI compliance:** Each device implements the command set from its respective programmer's reference manual. Short forms (e.g., `VOLT` for `VOLTAGE`, `MEAS` for `MEASURE`) are registered alongside long forms for compatibility with real test code.

**Simulation fidelity:** Measurements return the configured/injected values plus a small Gaussian noise term (≈1e-5 relative), mimicking real instrument behavior. You can override this with `inject(function, value)` for deterministic testing.

**Pure-Python fallback:** The SCPI parser has both a C++ and Python implementation. The Python version is always available; the C++ version improves throughput for high-rate command streaming.

**State isolation:** Each device instance maintains fully independent state. Running `*RST` returns all parameters to their power-on defaults without affecting other devices.

# Visual Regression Testing

The GUI is covered by **visual regression tests**: each test captures a
screenshot of a component and compares it pixel-for-pixel against a committed
*golden* reference image. A test fails when the difference exceeds a small
threshold, catching layout and paint regressions that ordinary assertions miss.

Tests live in `tests/visual/`. The shared helper is `compare_screenshot()` in
`tests/visual/conftest.py`.

## Running the tests

Everything runs in one command — visual tests are included automatically:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
pytest tests/ -v
```

**No `DISPLAY` and no `xvfb-run` prefix are required.** The repository's
top-level `tests/conftest.py` sets `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` before Qt is
imported, so Qt renders to an in-memory surface. On CI/EC2, `pytest-xvfb`
additionally starts a virtual X framebuffer automatically when the package is
installed. You never set `DISPLAY` by hand.

To run only the visual tests:

```bash
pytest tests/visual/ -v
```

## How golden images work

- Golden images live in `tests/visual/golden/` and **are committed** — they are
  the ground truth.
- On the **first** run of a new test, the golden is missing, so it is generated
  and saved automatically and the test passes. Commit the new golden.
- On **every later** run, the screenshot is compared against the golden and the
  test fails if the RMS pixel difference exceeds the threshold (default `5`).
- Diagnostic images go to `tests/visual/diffs/` and `tests/visual/actual/`,
  which are **git-ignored** — never commit them.

## Updating golden images after an intentional UI change

When you change the UI on purpose, the old goldens no longer match. Update them:

```bash
# Update one golden: delete it and re-run the test to regenerate
rm tests/visual/golden/main_window.png
pytest tests/visual/test_gui_main_window.py::test_main_window_opens

# Or update every golden at once
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 pytest tests/visual/
```

Then **review the regenerated images before committing** — a golden update is
only correct if the new rendering is what you intended:

```bash
git add tests/visual/golden/
git commit -m "chore(visual): update goldens after <describe UI change>"
```

Never commit a golden update without eyeballing the new image. A blindly
updated golden silently bakes in whatever regression you were supposed to catch.

## Reading a diff when a test fails

A failure prints the paths of three files in `tests/visual/diffs/`:

- `<name>_actual.png` — what the test rendered this run.
- `<name>_diff.png` — the per-pixel difference, **amplified 10×** so small
  changes are visible.
- The golden it was compared against (in `tests/visual/golden/`).

Open the actual and the golden side by side, and use the amplified diff to spot
*where* they differ. If the change is a real regression, fix the code. If the
change is intentional, update the golden (above).

## One-time EC2 / headless Linux setup

On a fresh headless Linux box (e.g. the overnight EC2 runner), Qt needs a few
system libraries and a virtual framebuffer. Run the setup script once:

```bash
./scripts/setup-visual-testing.sh
```

It installs `xvfb` and the Qt XCB runtime libraries via `apt-get`. After that,
`pip install -r requirements-dev.txt` (which includes `pytest-xvfb`) is all the
per-checkout setup needed, and `pytest tests/ -v` runs the full suite headlessly.

## Why the threshold is 5, not 0

Font hinting and antialiasing differ slightly between machines and Qt builds.
A threshold of `0` (pixel-perfect) would make tests flaky across environments;
`5` absorbs sub-pixel rendering noise while still catching real layout changes.
Generate goldens on the same platform the tests run on (the EC2 runner) so the
rendering matches as closely as possible.

#!/bin/bash
# One-time setup for running the GUI visual regression tests on a headless
# Linux machine (e.g. the overnight EC2 runner).
#
# Installs the Xvfb virtual framebuffer and the Qt XCB runtime libraries that
# PyQt6 needs. This is NOT a test runner — after running it once, the full
# suite (visual tests included) runs with a single command and no DISPLAY:
#
#   pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt
#   pytest tests/ -v
#
# pytest-xvfb (in requirements-dev.txt) starts Xvfb automatically; you never
# need an `xvfb-run` prefix or to set DISPLAY by hand.
set -euo pipefail

echo "Installing Xvfb and Qt XCB runtime libraries..."
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y \
  xvfb \
  libegl1 \
  libgl1 \
  libxkbcommon-x11-0 \
  libxcb-icccm4 \
  libxcb-image0 \
  libxcb-keysyms1 \
  libxcb-randr0 \
  libxcb-render-util0 \
  libxcb-xinerama0 \
  libxcb-shape0 \
  libxcb-cursor0 \
  libdbus-1-3 \
  libglib2.0-0

echo "Done. Now run:"
echo "  pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt"
echo "  pytest tests/ -v"

1	# Silmulator
2	
3	**SIL/HIL/CIL Hardware Simulator** — A PyQt6 GUI application for debugging embedded software against simulated lab instruments that behave per their real device specifications.
4	
5	## Documentation
6	
7	| Guide | Description |
8	|---|---|
9	| [User Guide](docs/user_guide.md) | Installation, quick start, virtual hardware reference, troubleshooting |
10	| [Developer Guide](docs/developer_guide.md) | Architecture, device layer, GUI layer, adding devices |
11	| [Adding Blocks](docs/adding_blocks.md) | Step-by-step guide to creating new hardware blocks |
12	| [Architecture Diagrams](docs/architecture.md) | Mermaid diagrams: system overview, data flow, class hierarchy |
13	| [Docker Guide](docker/README.md) | Browser (NoVNC) and native window Docker usage |
14	| [C++ Core](cpp_core/README.md) | SCPI parser build, API reference, Doxygen instructions |
15	| [Python Package](silmulator/README.md) | Package structure, library API reference |
16	| [Word User Guide](docs/Silmulator_User_Guide.docx) | Official Microsoft Word version for distribution |
17	
18	## Overview
19	
20	Silmulator provides a drag-and-drop canvas where you place virtual hardware blocks — oscilloscopes, power supplies, function generators, multimeters, and MSP430 microcontrollers — connect them with virtual wires, and interact with them using real SCPI commands. A code-input block parses your C/C++/Python source and routes the SCPI calls to the connected devices.
21	
22	This lets you test and debug measurement code **without physical hardware**, catching command errors and response-handling bugs at your desk.
23

34	│   ├── CMakeLists.txt
35	│   ├── include/
36	│   │   ├── scpi_parser.h          # Parser class declaration
37	│   │   └── scpi_types.h           # ScpiCommand, ScpiToken, etc.
38	│   └── src/
39	│       ├── scpi_parser.cpp        # Parser implementation
40	│       └── bindings.cpp           # pybind11 Python bindings
41	│

43	    ├── app.py                     # Application entry point
44	    ├── scpi/
45	    │   └── parser.py              # Pure-Python SCPI parser (fallback)
46	    ├── devices/

61	    │       ├── multimeter_block.py
62	    │       ├── msp430_block.py
63	    │       └── code_input_block.py
64	    ├── code_parser/
65	    │   └── base_parser.py         # C/C++/Python SCPI extractor
66	    └── utils/
67	        ├── waveform.py            # Waveform generation (numpy)

71	## Simulated Instruments
72	
73	### Oscilloscope (Tektronix MSO54-compatible)
74	- 4 analog channels (CH1–CH4)
75	- Full `ACQ`, `CH`, `CURSOR`, `DATA`, `DISPLAY`, `HORIZONTAL`, `MEASUREMENT`, `SELECT`, `TRIGGER`, `WFMPRE` command trees
76	- Waveform generation and `CURVE?` data transfer (ASCII and binary encoding)
77	- Live waveform injection via `inject_waveform(source, array)`
78	- 8 configurable measurements: FREQUENCY, PERIOD, AMPLITUDE, RMS, MEAN, HIGH, LOW, PK2PK, RISE, FALL, PDUTY, NDUTY
79	
80	### Power Supply (Keysight E36312A-compatible)
81	- 3 independent channels
82	- `SOURCE:VOLTAGE`, `SOURCE:CURRENT`, `OUTPUT`, `MEASURE`, `TRIGGER`, `INSTRUMENT` command trees
83	- OVP/OCP protection simulation
84	- `APPLY` combined set command
85	- Channel-by-channel tracking mode
86	
87	### Function Generator (Keysight 33522B-compatible)
88	- 2 independent channels (SOURCE1, SOURCE2)
89	- Functions: SIN, SQU, RAMP, PULS, NOIS, DC, USER, ARB
90	- AM, FM, PM, PWM modulation
91	- Burst and sweep modes
92	- Arbitrary waveform catalog
93	
94	### Multimeter (Keysight 34401A-compatible)
95	- Functions: VOLT:DC, VOLT:AC, CURR:DC, CURR:AC, RES, FRES, FREQ, PER, CONT, DIOD, TEMP
96	- `CONFIGURE`, `MEASURE`, `READ`, `FETCH`, `INITIATE` modes
97	- `CALCULATE` (null, limits, dB, statistics)
98	- `TRIGGER` and `SAMPLE` subsystems
99	- `DATA` buffer with `INITIATE`/`FETCH` workflow
100	- Measurement injection via `inject(function, value)`
101	
102	### MSP430 (TI MSP430FR5994-compatible)
103	- 8 GPIO ports (P1–P8) with direction, pull-up/down, interrupt control
104	- 12-channel 12-bit ADC with voltage injection
105	- 3x Timer_A, 1x Timer_B with capture-compare
106	- 4x UART (eUSCI_A) with full serial config
107	- 2x SPI (eUSCI_B) with CPOL/CPHA and transfer simulation
108	- 4x I2C with address, frequency, master/slave modes
109	- Unified Clock System (DCO, LFXT, SMCLK, MCLK, ACLK)
110	- Power management modes (AM, LPM0–LPM4.5)
111	- 16-register CPU state, PC control, memory map read/write
112	
113	## SCPI Command Examples
114	
115	```python
116	from silmulator.devices import Oscilloscope, PowerSupply, FunctionGenerator
117	
118	# Oscilloscope
119	osc = Oscilloscope()
120	osc.process("CH1:SCALE 0.5")           # 500mV/div
121	osc.process("HOR:SCALE 1E-3")          # 1ms/div
122	osc.process("TRIG:A:EDGE:SOURCE CH1")
123	osc.process("TRIG:A:LEVEL 1.5")
124	osc.process("ACQ:STATE 1")             # Run
125	freq = osc.process("MEASUREMENT:MEAS1:TYPE FREQUENCY; VALUE?")
126	data = osc.process("CURVE?")           # Get waveform data
127	
128	# Power Supply
129	psu = PowerSupply()
130	psu.process("INST:NSEL 1")
131	psu.process("VOLT 3.3")
132	psu.process("CURR 1.0")
133	psu.process("OUTP ON")
134	voltage = psu.process("MEAS:VOLT:DC?")
135	
136	# Function Generator
137	fgen = FunctionGenerator()
138	fgen.process("SOURCE1:FUNC SIN")
139	fgen.process("SOURCE1:FREQ 1000")
140	fgen.process("SOURCE1:VOLT 2.0")
141	fgen.process("OUTPUT1 ON")
142	
143	# MSP430
144	mcu = MSP430()
145	mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:DIRECTION 0xFF")  # All outputs
146	mcu.process("GPIO:PORT1:OUTPUT 0x01")     # P1.0 HIGH
147	mcu.process("ADC:CHANNEL0:INJECT 1.65")  # Inject 1.65V
148	raw = mcu.process("ADC:CONVERT 0")       # Read raw ADC value
149	```

152	
153	The C++ SCPI parser (`cpp_core/`) provides a high-performance parsing backend with pybind11 Python bindings. It is optional — the pure-Python `silmulator/scpi/parser.py` is used automatically when the C++ extension is not built.

182	```
